title: Elon Musk on Rogan #2404: testing to failure, incentives, and betting on AI and robotics
summary: Wide-ranging 2025 Rogan interview. Musk explains why Starship is deliberately pushed to failure in testing, why full reusability cuts launch costs by 100x or more, why he chose to participate in AI rather than spectate, and why incentives explain behavior. Much of the rest is political commentary.

principles.text: Deliberately push hardware past normal limits in development so it is safe when it carries people or valuable cargo.
principles.quote: we intentionally subject it to uh uh you know a flight regime that is much worse than what we expect in normal flight so that when we put people on board or valuable cargo it doesn't blow up.

principles.text: Full reusability is the step-change that collapses cost, as with any mode of transport.
principles.quote: full reusability um uh drops the cost of access to space by a hundred um maybe even more than 100 actually. So could be like a thousand.

principles.text: To understand any behavior, look at the incentives behind it.
principles.quote: If if you want to understand behavior, you have to look at the incentives.

principles.text: Be a participant, not a spectator, if you want to influence where a technology goes.
principles.quote: really there's two choices here. Either be a spectator or a or a participant. And if I'm a spectator, I can't really influence the direction of AI.

principles.text: Make products look distinct and evolve the aesthetic over time rather than leaving it static.
principles.quote: I think we want to change the aesthetic over time. You don't want the aesthetic to be constant over time. You want to evolve the aesthetic.

principles.text: AI safety hinges on keeping AI maximally truth-seeking rather than forcing it to believe falsehoods.
principles.quote: the most important thing is that it be maximally truth seeeking like that you don't force the AI to believe things that are false.
